methodologyNotes: Roster covers thirteen WiFi/USB-C and standalone-screen ear-cleaning (visual ear-wax-removal) cameras, verified 2026-08-12 against manufacturer/official-storefront pages (bebird.com, teslong.com, supereyes-store.com, anykit.com) where available, corroborated by retailer listings (Amazon, Walmart, RehabMart, Desertcart) where a direct manufacturer page did not exist or could not be fetched in full; three seed entries required correction. "Bebird Note5 Pro", "Bebird X17 Pro", "Bebird M9 Pro", and "Bebird R3" are legacy/incorrect names — Bebird's current official catalog (bebird.com) sells this line as the "EarSight" series with no "Pro" suffix and no X17 or R3 SKU at all, so the four seeds were mapped to their closest current real equivalents: EarSight Note 5, EarSight Ultra X (current flagship, successor to the X-series), EarSight M9, and EarSight R1 (entry model; R3 does not exist in any generation of the lineup). "Axel Glade Spade Pro" could not be verified as a real product or brand under any spelling via manufacturer search, retailer search, or general web search and was dropped as fictional/mis-transcribed; "Coolour Ear Camera" and "KLseagon Otoscope" were likewise unverifiable as real ear-camera brands (searches under both names return zero relevant manufacturer or retail listings) and were dropped. To hold the roster at a useful size, three real, independently verified substitute SKUs were added in their place: a second Anykit model (the 4.5in-screen gyroscope otoscope, distinct from Anykit's WiFi SA39W model already in the roster), and NIUTA's 1296P wireless ear camera (a genuine Walmart-listed product surfaced while searching for "KLseagon", used here since Walmart's bot-detection blocked full page-body retrieval, so its specs come from the indexed listing title/description rather than a rendered spec table). Depstech's own otoscopes collection page (depstech.com/collections/otoscopes) currently returns zero listed products, so the Depstech entry is sourced from its Amazon listing (ASIN B0D17949NR) instead, with several fields left null because Amazon's bot-blocking prevented full spec-table retrieval — the same null-over-guess approach was applied to the Wsky R1 entry (ASIN B09ZY6HM6H), whose brand attribution and specs rest on title text only, not a confirmed rendered detail page. Standalone-screen devices (Teslong MS450D39, the second Anykit model, Yinama's 4.3in unit) have connectivity and app_compatibility marked as not applicable/none since they operate without a phone app or WiFi link, unlike the WiFi-to-smartphone models that make up most of the category. accessedAt 2026-08-12 throughout.
